title: Cauliflower: modeled ₹402/qtl left, Una → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: January 2024: reported cauliflower prices at Una and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 96% of 23 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹402 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 1,304 same-variety market pairs screened for cauliflower in January 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2024
scenes.caption: Una (Himachal Pradesh) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported cauliflower prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 23 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Una reported a median ₹1,600 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹2,375 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹575/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹575 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 96% of days.

scenes.headline: 93 km by road
scenes.caption: 93 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~2 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹20/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹369 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹278 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 19 of 23 modeled shipping days. 19 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹402 per quintal (₹289 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Cauliflower route from Una to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 96% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹40,200, or ₹28,900 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to cauliflower
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹20/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Cauliflower route from Una to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 96% of matched days in January 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹40,200, or ₹28,900 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
